title: Layered Architecture Technical Reference
readerIntent: Map a technical artifact to its responsibility and validation expectations.
owner: Nodics modular runtime and all module owners
summary: The technical hierarchy is consistent across modules even when a small module does not require every optional layer.

sections.heading: Ownership rules
items: Every artifact has one reason to change and one owning capability. Schemas own shape, services own behavior, controllers own transport adaptation, and providers own vendor mapping.
Generated files are derived and not hand-authored; temporary root docs are planning material and not runtime or canonical implemented documentation.
Dependencies point from application coordination toward stable framework contracts without circular group imports or direct access to another module's persistence.

sections.heading: Layered customization
items: Reuse existing behavior first, customize properties second, extend the smallest supported service or schema third, and create a new implementation only when required.
A customer project layers modules beside the reusable Nodics framework so two applications can customize the same base service independently.
Do not copy whole modules, edit vendor adapters from business code, add parallel loaders, or put frontend renderers inside backend repositories.

sections.heading: Runtime composition
items: Modules compose in monoServer or distributed topology through the same contracts. Server layout is deployment choice rather than business ownership.
Direct module communication uses configured logical endpoints and authenticated service or human identity; BackOffice registry assists discovery but is not a data proxy.
Lifecycle hooks, readiness, drain, observability, and provider cleanup remain bounded contributions to the single process lifecycle.

sections.heading: Review and verification
items: Review placement, dependency direction, authority duplication, configuration location, generated boundaries, security, observability, testing, and beginner documentation.
Test framework defaults, customer overrides, two projects with different overrides, mono and distributed runtime, provider substitution, upgrade, rollback, and regression.
Automated structure checks support review but do not justify meaningless scaffold code or modifications to blank module templates.

sections.heading: Artifact map
items: config: properties, definitions, presets, and lifecycle scripts.
src/schema and src/search: governed data and query contracts.
src/service and src/facade: owned behavior and use-case coordination.
src/controller and src/router: transport adaptation and API declarations.
src/pipelines and src/interceptors: ordered processing and explicit lifecycle extensions.
src/event: event declarations, listeners, and handlers.
src/lib and src/utils: narrow reusable mechanics.
src/status: stable success and error definitions.
test: focused contracts plus integration and regression evidence.

sections.heading: Dependency direction
paragraphs: Higher-level use-case and transport layers depend on owned services and contracts. Provider adapters implement provider-neutral framework contracts. Business modules do not reach around those contracts to bind directly to infrastructure clients.
